text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Winding up a four-day visit to Malaysia on Tuesday, Prime Minister Gyula Horn encouraged the Southeast Asian nation to open an office in Budapest in a bid to promote exports.
- Completing a two-day official visit to Budapest on Tuesday, Croatian President Franjo Tudjman envisaged offering Croatian citizenship to ethnic Croats living in Hungary.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs wrapped up talks in Tokyo on Tuesday and proceeds to Vietnam today.

- The government is set to discuss a Ministry of Agriculture proposal on the handling of potato surplus this week. State Secretary at the Ministry Fulop Benedek indicated there is a good chance of Hungary reaching a consensus with the four countries which lodged a complaint against Hungary's agricultural subsidies with the WTO.

- Parliament passed a bill on Tuesday on the protection of children and amendments to the Act on Bankruptcy and Liquidation Proceedings. Parliament opened debate on a proposal for amending the Customs Act.
- The general meeting of the Pension Insurance Authority severely criticised the government's pension reform scheme on Tuesday.

- The Constitutional Court ruled on Tuesday that it will be a constitutional requirement for the state or local governments to extend a supplementary subsidy toward the operation of public education institutions maintained by churches.

- Entrepreneurs were able to take out loans of less than 12 months' maturity at 22.8 percent interest in February, and longer-term loans at 24.3 percent, some 7.6 percent less than a year earlier, the National Bank of Hungary reports.
- The third stage of the reconstruction of Budapest's Nagykorut will continue from May 2.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Besides the expected sale of its Vienna-based subsidiary CW Bank, the National Bank of Hungary is set to sell its 34 percent stake in the CIB this year.
- A Slovak consortium and the German company Alcher have submitted bids for the Ozd-based steel works Ozdi Acelmuvek Rt.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The Ministry of Industry projects a foreign trade deficit of $3.5-4 billion this year, as opposed to the $2.9-3 billion forecast by the Ministry of Finance.

- Some 961 companies were founded with foreign capital of a total of 5.3 billion forints in the first quarter, 58 percent less than in the same period of last year, reports the Central Statistical Office.
- The Hungarian Electricity Works broke even last year on net sales of 178.6 billion forints, 39.9 billion less than a year earlier, preliminary calculations reveal.
- The Hungarian telecommunications firm Matav will start commercial distribution of Internet services on May 5.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Finance Ministry State Secretary Laszlo Akar said Hungary seeks a new form of co-operation with the IMF as the country does not intend to draw loans from the financial institution once its standby credit agreement expires at the end of the year.
